title: Near-Universal Dual Wolbachia Infection in Portuguese Aedes albopictus Provides a Molecular Baseline for Incompatible Insect Technique
content: Aedes albopictus, a vector of several arboviruses, has recently invaded Europe, including Portugal, raising public health concern. Wolbachia-based incompatible insect technique (IIT) requires prior knowledge of the resident infection. We screened 344 mosquitoes from Lisbon, Olhão and Penafiel (Portugal; 2024–2025) for wAlbA and wAlbB, typed 15 individuals by five-locus multilocus sequence typing (MLST), sequenced mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase I (COI) from 69 specimens (83 including GenBank sequences), and assembled complete Nanopore mitogenomes of two isofemale lines from Lisbon (JBL) and Olhão (OLH). Wolbachia was detected in 341/344 mosquitoes (99.1%): 327 (95.1%) carried both strains, 13 (3.8%) only wAlbB, one only wAlbA, three were uninfected. Single wAlbB infections were concentrated in males (12/141 vs. 1/203 females; P < 0.001). All sites shared wAlbA ST-2 and wAlbB ST-464. COI diversity was moderate (haplotype/nucleotide diversity 0.636/0.00133) in a star-like network. The JBL and OLH mitogenomes matched two mitochondrial lineages previously reported from southern Portugal (A1a1a1b and A1a), corresponding to COI haplotypes H6 and H7. Portuguese Ae. albopictus thus carry a uniform, high-prevalence dual infection across at least two maternal lineages, providing the first molecular baseline for Wolbachia-based IIT strain selection in Portugal, pending experimental cytoplasmic incompatibility verification.
